thinkBeforeYouCode.question: What is the difference in memory between an instance field and a static field?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: An instance field (like name) is allocated inside every single object on the Heap. A static field (like nextIdCounter) is allocated only once in the Metaspace/Class area and is shared by all instances of that class.

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: Why should static methods NOT access instance variables like this.name directly?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: A static method belongs to the class itself, not to any individual object. Because it can be called when zero objects exist (e.g. CourseSection.printGlobalStats()), there is no 'this' instance to read fields from.

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: Why use public static final for constants?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: public makes it readable everywhere; static means one copy is shared rather than duplicating memory in every instance; final guarantees that no one can change the constant at runtime.

# Student ID & Course Registration (Java OOP)

## Overview
A university registration engine in Java demonstrating the distinction between class-level `static` state and instance-level state, featuring auto-incrementing ID generation and capacity enforcement.

## Architecture Blueprint
```
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                             EnrolledStudent                             |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| - static counter: int = 0                                               |
| - studentId: final String                                               |
| - name: String                                                          |
| - email: String                                                         |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| + EnrolledStudent(name: String, email: String)                          |
| + static getTotalStudentsCreated(): int                                 |
| + getStudentId(): String                                                |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                              CourseSection                              |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| + static final MAX_CAPACITY: int = 3                                    |
| - static totalEnrollments: int = 0                                      |
| - courseCode: String                                                    |
| - courseTitle: String                                                   |
| - enrolledStudents: List<EnrolledStudent>                               |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| + CourseSection(code: String, title: String)                            |
| + enroll(student: EnrolledStudent): boolean                             |
| + static getTotalEnrollments(): int                                     |
| + printRoster(): void                                                   |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Key Architectural Patterns
- **Auto-Incrementing Sequence**: Private `static int counter` safely stamps consecutive IDs (`STU-2026-0001`, `STU-2026-0002`).
- **Static Final Constants**: `MAX_CAPACITY` defines an immutable class-wide ceiling.
- **Global Synchronization**: `totalEnrollments` tracks multi-section metrics across independent course objects.

## How to Run
```bash
javac EnrolledStudent.java CourseSection.java EnrollmentApp.java
java EnrollmentApp
```

## Sample Console Output
```text
=======================================================
           COURSE SECTION ROSTER: CS101               
               Introduction to Java                    
=======================================================
Capacity: 3 | Enrolled: 3 | Status: SECTION FULL
-------------------------------------------------------
 1. STU-2026-0001 | Alice Walker   | alice@campus.edu
 2. STU-2026-0002 | Bob Martinez   | bob@campus.edu
 3. STU-2026-0003 | Charlie Zhang  | charlie@campus.edu
=======================================================
Attempting to enroll Student STU-2026-0004...
Error: Cannot enroll. CS101 has reached MAX_CAPACITY (3).
```

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: What is the difference in memory between an instance field and a static field?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: An instance field (like name) is allocated inside every single object on the Heap. A static field (like nextIdCounter) is allocated only once in the Metaspace/Class area and is shared by all instances of that class.

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: Why should static methods NOT access instance variables like this.name directly?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: A static method belongs to the class itself, not to any individual object. Because it can be called when zero objects exist (e.g. CourseSection.printGlobalStats()), there is no 'this' instance to read fields from.

thinkBeforeYouCode.question: Why use public static final for constants?
thinkBeforeYouCode.mentorInsight: public makes it readable everywhere; static means one copy is shared rather than duplicating memory in every instance; final guarantees that no one can change the constant at runtime.

# Student ID & Course Registration (Java OOP)

## Overview
A university registration engine in Java demonstrating the distinction between class-level `static` state and instance-level state, featuring auto-incrementing ID generation and capacity enforcement.

## Architecture Blueprint
```
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                             EnrolledStudent                             |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| - static counter: int = 0                                               |
| - studentId: final String                                               |
| - name: String                                                          |
| - email: String                                                         |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| + EnrolledStudent(name: String, email: String)                          |
| + static getTotalStudentsCreated(): int                                 |
| + getStudentId(): String                                                |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                              CourseSection                              |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| + static final MAX_CAPACITY: int = 3                                    |
| - static totalEnrollments: int = 0                                      |
| - courseCode: String                                                    |
| - courseTitle: String                                                   |
| - enrolledStudents: List<EnrolledStudent>                               |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| + CourseSection(code: String, title: String)                            |
| + enroll(student: EnrolledStudent): boolean                             |
| + static getTotalEnrollments(): int                                     |
| + printRoster(): void                                                   |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

## Key Architectural Patterns
- **Auto-Incrementing Sequence**: Private `static int counter` safely stamps consecutive IDs (`STU-2026-0001`, `STU-2026-0002`).
- **Static Final Constants**: `MAX_CAPACITY` defines an immutable class-wide ceiling.
- **Global Synchronization**: `totalEnrollments` tracks multi-section metrics across independent course objects.

## How to Run
```bash
javac EnrolledStudent.java CourseSection.java EnrollmentApp.java
java EnrollmentApp
```

## Sample Console Output
```text
=======================================================
           COURSE SECTION ROSTER: CS101               
               Introduction to Java                    
=======================================================
Capacity: 3 | Enrolled: 3 | Status: SECTION FULL
-------------------------------------------------------
 1. STU-2026-0001 | Alice Walker   | alice@campus.edu
 2. STU-2026-0002 | Bob Martinez   | bob@campus.edu
 3. STU-2026-0003 | Charlie Zhang  | charlie@campus.edu
=======================================================
Attempting to enroll Student STU-2026-0004...
Error: Cannot enroll. CS101 has reached MAX_CAPACITY (3).
```
